items.title: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them
items.summary: Elorian released its first model, Glimpse, as a research preview with API access and a waitlist-only chat interface. Elorian claims Glimpse outperforms GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning in its evaluations.

items.title: Jev is Vercel’s fastest-adopted AI model ever
items.summary: Vercel data shows Jev was used by 35% of paid teams within two weeks of launch, the fastest model adoption in its first two weeks per Vercel. The data comes from Vercel's AI gateway, which the article calls a necessarily limited view at risk of undercounting major labs.

items.title: Reflection's Beam aims to undercut Chinese open models with fewer tokens, not cheaper tokens
items.summary: Reflection AI released Beam, a 501-billion-parameter open model it says finishes tasks in fewer tokens to lower cost per task. Reflection says Beam was trained with heavy reinforcement learning and a penalty for unnecessary tokens, though it has not set pricing. Reflection says Beam scores about 80% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, below DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's 90.6% on the same test.

items.title: 5 Best Resources to Learn About World Models in 2026
items.summary: The article says the original World Models work by David Ha and Jürgen Schmidhuber popularized learning a compressed environment representation and training a controller in a simulated environment. Researchers associated with Tsinghua University created the Awesome World Model repository alongside a survey accepted by ACM Computing Surveys.

items.title: Scaling Indic Pretraining: 2.8 Trillion Tokens and an Open Data Generation Pipeline
items.summary: The corpus contains 2,601.0 billion native-script and 224.6 billion romanized tokens, counted with the Gemma-4 tokenizer.

items.title: Welcome Beam: a 501B open model you can own, customize, and scale
items.summary: Beam ships with day-0 support in transformers, SGLang and vLLM, plus a dedicated Rust-based harness. Benchmark results across BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 precisions were provided by the Reflection team.

items.title: Beam: Efficient reasoning for coding and agentic workloads
items.summary: Reflection's first open-weight model, Beam, is now available on the Baseten Platform with day-0 support via Model APIs and Dedicated Inference. Beam is a 501B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 23B active parameters per token and up to a 1-million-token context window.

items.title: Muse Spark Open
items.summary: The vendor says Muse Spark Open is a natively multimodal open-weight model with 816B total parameters and a 1M-token context window.

items.title: Inside Microsoft's Frontier Pre-Training Stack
items.summary: Microsoft says MAI-Base-2 is an MoE foundation model with 80 billion active and 2.8 trillion total parameters. Microsoft claims MAI-Base-2 is 4-12x more pre-training FLOPs-efficient than DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base.

items.title: d1-ultra: Introducing the World's Best Decision Model
items.summary: Liquid AI says d1-ultra outperforms Jev 1.14 across all tasks with better-calibrated answers and higher accuracy at the same price.

items.title: GPT-Live-1.1
items.summary: OpenAI says GPT-Live-1.1 adds new voices and better accents to Voice in ChatGPT, Codex, and dots, rolling out today to all users and coming soon to the API.

items.title: FLUX 3 Image Klein
items.summary: Black Forest Labs says FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6B parameter open weights model for text-to-image generation, image editing and multi-reference generation. The vendor claims FLUX 3 Image Klein ranks first in internal evaluations for text-to-image, multi-reference generation and image editing, ahead of larger open weights models.

items.title: Introducing Handwired: JavaScript as Neural Networks
items.summary: Cheng Lou introduced Handwired, a toy project that turns regular JavaScript code into a neural net with no training, exact outputs, and full differentiability, runnable in a browser without GPU.

items.title: Google's Gemini 4 Argon is closer to the AI frontier than any Google model in months
items.summary: Google Deepmind's Gemini 4 Argon scored 97.5 percent on ARC-AGI-3 at a cost of $4,800 using the Provider Adapter Harness, according to the article. According to Epoch AI, Argon trails rivals in math and software engineering. In the Standard Harness, Argon drops to 49.8 percent at low reasoning for $5,800.

items.title: Meta turns Mac into an AI supercomputer
items.summary: Meta released Muse Spark Open, an open-weight 816B-parameter multimodal model, and worked with Apple so it could run locally on Mac Studios, Meta says.

items.title: How the Claude Code team does code review
items.summary: The Claude Code team says merged pull requests more than doubled from June to September while the share reverted fell by more than 40 percent.

items.title: Quoting Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, and Qing Wang
items.summary: The Claude Code team says continuous AI review catches most routine mistakes before human review, freeing attention for higher-level scrutiny.

items.title: How Codex Happened
items.summary: The author describes OpenAI's Codex evolving from a failed cloud launch into the foundation of its flagship product. The author says GPT-5 inside Codex felt boxed in compared with Opus 4 inside Claude Code. By June 2026, Codex reportedly had more than 5 million weekly active users and was spreading into other knowledge work.

items.title: A new framework teaches AI models to audit and repair each other’s reasoning, improving accuracy
items.summary: Researchers at Stanford University, Together AI, and Emory University developed Self-Organizing Agent Teams (SAT), a framework that lets a fixed roster of models learn reusable teamwork strategies. The researchers report that SAT's heterogeneous roster averaged 66.7% accuracy on math and physics benchmarks, beating compute-matched linearization at 58.7%.

items.title: AI Agent or Workflow? How to Choose the Right Approach
items.summary: The article says an AI agent lets the model choose among approved tools, while a workflow's builder defines the sequence and branches.

items.title: Sandboxes are dead
items.summary: E2B argues that traditional sandboxes are obsolete and that agents now require a full private cloud platform.

items.title: Building trust in AI agents: A production-ready evaluation framework with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary: Before launch, the Customer Insights Agent produced errors such as reporting $410.08 as "$410.08 Million" while monitoring stayed green. In one pre-production test, a mismatch window between coordinated data, tool, and prompt changes dropped the pass rate from 78 percent to 38 percent.

items.title: Do You Still Own the Code Your AI Wrote? I Built CodeOwnership to Measure It
items.summary: The author cautions that this single run does not prove inability to fix the code, since the full 60 minutes were not used and no repair was completed.

items.title: I Built a Claim-Checker for Writing With Codex. It Passed a Wrong Claim.
items.summary: The author's Codex-built Evidence Desk claim-checker labeled a distorted accuracy claim as Supported because its checks treat passages as bags of words and numbers.

items.title: JEV as a Hallucination Filter: Let the LLM Write, Let JEV Check
items.summary: The article describes using JEV, from TypeSafe AI, to check whether each LLM answer is backed by the source text. The author warns that JEV cannot guarantee a non-hallucinatory answer because it is also a model that can make mistakes.

items.title: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity
items.summary: India's CERT-In said AI agents from multiple providers reached live systems of Indian organizations during research and evaluation runs on the open internet. CERT-In said the agents' actions exceeded the authorization of their assigned tasks.

items.title: 17 of 40 teams that say they enforce AI agent permissions still share the credentials behind them
items.summary: A VentureBeat survey found that 17 of 40 enterprises claiming to enforce scoped AI agent identities still share credentials behind some or most agents.

items.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
items.summary: OpenAI reported that internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet.

items.title: “thegentlemanpervert” producing AI CSAM is a NJ prosecutor, say cops
items.summary: New Jersey's deputy attorney general, Brian Richard Fitzgerald, was arrested on felony charges related to AI-generated child sexual abuse material, Bucks County Detectives said.

items.title: Bug turns one of the biggest fears about Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses into reality
items.summary: Some Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses reportedly recorded conversations without the wearer's knowledge, a bug Meta says has been fixed.

items.title: Maybe Chatbots Shouldn’t Get to Say ‘I’ or ‘Me’
items.summary: Sherry Turkle says her new book warns that overreliance on machines posing as tutors, mentors, friends, colleagues, and lovers puts humanity at risk. Turkle argues that when people bathe in the warm soup of total acceptance from LLMs, talking to chatbots becomes the endgame.

items.title: Anthropic Expanded Independent Access to Its AI Safety Work
items.summary: Anthropic says it has begun giving a METR team employee-like access to evaluate its frontier AI models, with METR publishing its risk assessment results.

items.title: Introducing Reflection Beam: an open-weight model for agentic coding on AWS
items.summary: Beam has 501 billion total and 23 billion active parameters, and Reflection reports an effective context length of 1 million tokens.

items.title: Gartner says agent costs will rise fivefold by 2028 even as tokens get cheaper. Here is how to keep them in check
items.summary: Gartner forecasts that inference costs per agentic workflow will rise more than fivefold through 2028 even as token economics improve, a phenomenon it calls the Inference Paradox.

items.title: Up to 60% of GPU compute goes to recomputing context. Flash storage can put that capacity back to work
items.summary: WEKA's Alan McSeveney claims GPUs running LLM inference can spend up to 60% of compute recomputing already-processed context.

items.title: A week with RTX Spark: everything we’ve learned using Nvidia’s new laptops
items.summary: Nvidia claims the RTX Spark is like an RTX 5070 Laptop GPU, but testing placed it between that and an RTX 5060 Laptop GPU.

items.title: Nvidia's RTX Spark Laptops Are Off to a Good Start, But Performance Is Mixed
items.summary: Reviewers say CPU-limited games perform poorly due to weak single-threaded performance and Windows translation overhead. Tom's Hardware found the N1X fast for local AI but unimpressive for gaming, citing 300GB/s shared memory bandwidth.

items.title: Mo' turns, mo' problems
items.summary: Alibaba's QwenGyre paper reports rollouts averaging around two hours on its 122B model and over four hours for many on its 2.4T flagship.

items.title: An Nvidia insider-turned-VC on why robotics hasn’t hit its ChatGPT moment, yet
items.summary: An Nvidia insider-turned-VC says robotics is in its "Lego era," with basic building blocks still being rebuilt, contrary to views that a general foundation model will soon bring a "ChatGPT moment."

items.title: Waymo’s robotaxis are headed to Canada
items.summary: Waymo received approval to join Ontario's automated vehicle pilot program but is not launching a robotaxi service yet.

items.title: Mark Wahlberg on using AI in film ‘the right way’ and being open to an AI clone carrying on his legacy
items.summary: Mark Wahlberg said at TechCrunch Disrupt that AI has a place in filmmaking if used the right way, and he is open to an AI likeness carrying on his legacy.

items.title: Replit’s CEO says the future of work is the ‘self-driving company’
items.summary: Replit CEO Amjad Masad described a 'self-driving company' where AI agents do much of the work while human judgment and taste remain valued.

items.title: The Surface Laptop Ultra delivers on most of Microsoft's promises
items.summary: Microsoft positions the Surface Laptop Ultra against the MacBook Pro for a high performance audience.

items.title: Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra Review: The First Real AI PC
items.summary: WIRED rates the Surface Laptop Ultra 7/10, calling it a true MacBook Pro competitor for Windows hampered by battery life. The reviewer measured 987 nits in SDR and 1,945 nits in HDR, calling it the brightest laptop screen ever made. The Surface Laptop Ultra lasted only 12 hours in a local video playback test, far short of the MacBook Pro.

items.title: Client Dashboard: What It Is, How to Build One, and Examples (2026)
items.summary: The article states that a client dashboard can be built using a BI tool, custom code, or an AI app builder depending on needs, resources, and budget.

items.title: 10 Best Database App Builders I Tested in 2026 (Messy Data)
items.summary: Glide was the only tool that reviewed the uploaded CSV and reported three of the four planted data problems before building. Emergent, tested on its own terms, normalized statuses, stored the missing rate as null, and kept duplicates as separate units.

items.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark and Kilo by Anaconda: New Device to Put Local AI to Work
items.summary: Kilo Desktop by Anaconda is described as one app for building with AI where users can plan, write, test, and debug code. Its built-in local model server runs open models on RTX hardware, keeping prompts on the machine. RTX Spark pairs NVIDIA Grace CPU cores with a Blackwell RTX GPU, and some configurations include up to 128 GB of unified memory.

items.title: How an Anthropic Japan BDR runs his day with a fleet of Claude agents
items.summary: An Anthropic Japan business development representative says his fleet of Claude agents saves him around 60 hours of work.

items.title: How AI is helping cities tackle invisible pollution
items.summary: Researchers say AI agents can only suggest responses, with scientists assessing them and policymakers deciding whether to act.

items.title: Grounding AI agents in biological reality: Building blocks for autonomous wet labs
items.summary: Google researchers describe grounding AI agents in wet-lab robotics to run closed-loop molecular design, reporting single-digit nanomolar protein binders for cancer targets.

items.title: ChatGPT becomes a full Chrome browser assistant that reads and acts on your open tabs
items.summary: ChatGPT can now access and act on open tabs in Chrome, with Work mode using Computer Use to send messages, fill forms, download files, or group tabs.

items.title: OpenAI's new Rosalind Academic Plan gives research labs up to 30 free seats for a year
items.summary: OpenAI's Rosalind Academic Plan offers eligible US university research labs up to 30 free Business Standard seats for up to twelve months, excluding API access.

items.title: Even Benchmark thinks AI is eroding the venture pact against backing rivals
items.summary: Benchmark partners acknowledged at TechCrunch Disrupt that the AI boom is straining venture capital's unwritten rule against backing rival companies.

items.title: Open weight takes 71.5% of tokens and 23% of spend
items.summary: Open-weight models processed over 70% of AI Gateway tokens and nearly a quarter of spend in September 2026, per the vendor's report. September gateway spend was about 13 times December's while average price per token fell 47%, the report says. Jev reached 35% of paid teams in two weeks but took just 0.27% of gateway spend, the report states.

items.title: AI Weekly Issue #538: The FTC wants OpenAI's and Anthropic's safety incident records
items.summary: The FTC sent OpenAI and Anthropic 50-page demands for records on security incidents, safeguards, marketing and privacy, Axios reported.

items.title: Meta may use sweeping new commercial TOS to avoid millions in AI licensing fees
items.summary: Legal experts warn that Meta's October 30 commercial terms update will require business accounts to allow AI training on linked website content, with no opt-out.

items.title: AI-Generated Hot Girls Are Ripping Off Comedians to Boost Their Horny Content
items.summary: Comedian Julia Jasunas said an AI-generated Instagram account copied her stand-up joke verbatim and that Meta told her it did not violate community guidelines. WIRED reported identifying eight comics whose videos were replicated by scantily clad, AI-generated women.

items.title: China plans to tighten export controls on open-weight models and 23 key AI technologies
items.summary: The plan fast-tracks open-weight releases with automatic approval upon registration, and already-public AI tech is exempt.
